new_entities.name: Topical adapalene 0.1%
new_entities.description: Topical adapalene 0.1% formulations used as acne treatment.

new_entities.name: Clinical moderate acne
new_entities.description: Clinically assessed mild-to-moderate or moderate acne vulgaris severity and lesion burden.

edges.effect_quant: The largest placebo-controlled adapalene 0.1% programme randomized 2,141 subjects and found significantly better investigator-rated success and lesion-count reduction than vehicle at 12 weeks. Smaller practice-based studies and review-level evidence reinforce that adapalene 0.1% is clinically effective and generally well tolerated for mild-to-moderate acne.
edges.population: adolescents and adults with mild-to-moderate or moderate acne vulgaris treated with adapalene 0.1%
edges.mechanism: Adapalene normalizes follicular keratinization and reduces inflammatory acne activity while generally causing less irritation than older topical retinoids, which helps adherence.
edges.summary: Topical adapalene 0.1% is a well-supported first-line acne retinoid rather than a speculative cosmeceutical. The evidence is not novel, but it is strong enough and consistent enough to support a beneficial classification for moderate acne control.
edges.caveats: Adapalene often works best within combination regimens, and it can still irritate sensitive skin. This edge is about clinical acne improvement, not immediate cosmetic clearing.
